text: What's inside an AirPod? We scaled one up a hundred times, and took it apart.
Crack the glued shell, and every part comes out.
First, the battery: a tiny lithium-ion button cell. In AirPods Pro 2, about fifty milliamp-hours.
The main chip runs Bluetooth and processes the sound. A thin antenna catches the signal from your phone.
Now the speaker. A copper voice coil sits around a magnet. Pulse current through it, and the coil pushes the diaphragm back and forth, thousands of times a second.
Beamforming mics aim at your voice, and a tiny vent equalizes pressure, so your ear doesn't feel plugged.
A force sensor in the stem feels your squeeze, and a skin sensor knows when it's in your ear.
Now, noise cancellation. The outer mic hears the noise. The chip flips that wave upside down, and the driver plays it. Peak meets trough, and they cancel out.
Apple says it re-tunes that two hundred times a second.
The catch? It's all glued shut. iFixit gave them zero out of ten for repairability.
What should we take apart next?
Congrats! You've discovered what's inside your earbuds.
